comment: CI shard map for the e2e job (parallel: 9). Each entry lists the feature FILES one shard runs (comma-separated, relative to the codecept dir, consumed via TASK_CODECEPTJS_FEATURES); check:shard-coverage enforces that every feature file lands in exactly one shard. Balanced on measured CI durations: the long single stories ride alone (1, 2) and bound the pipeline wall-clock; the MegaLinter-hungry pair shares shard 7 so its image pull is paid once and both run concurrently. Runner-driven stories register a project-scoped runner on the shard's OWN gitlab-runner service (each CI shard boots its own compose stack), so they need not share a shard — they are spread instead: shard 9 keeps @daily-contribution and @release-window (~18 min together), shard 5 takes @test-discipline. Grouping all three cost 11 extra minutes of wall-clock, because one runner slot serialised their pipelines. A LOCAL full-suite run ignores this map and shares one runner service, which is why the teardown stays surgical.
